evidence.snippet: This review provides evidence to reinforce the previous hypothesis that missense mutations in exons 1-12 and mutations leading to a premature stop codon lead to the severe form of the disease, while missense pathogenic variants in exons 13-17 lead to the mild form of the disease.

meta.presence: Biallelic loss-of-function variants, homozygous or compound heterozygous

nodes.description: Both ANTXR2 alleles carry a loss-of-function change: a missense substitution in the extracellular von Willebrand factor A or immunoglobulin-like domain, a frameshift or nonsense change, or a splice variant. The founding study mapped the locus to chromosome 4q21 and found 15 different such changes across 17 families covering both the mild and the severe presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding capillary morphogenesis protein 2 cause juvenile hyaline fibromatosis and infantile systemic hyalinosis.
evidence.snippet: We previously mapped the gene for JHF to chromosome 4q21. We now report the identification of 15 different mutations in the gene encoding capillary morphogenesis protein 2 (CMG2) in 17 families with JHF or ISH.

genetic_context.description: Germline and biallelic. Homozygous in the consanguineous families that make up much of the literature, compound heterozygous otherwise.

nodes.description: Intralesional or oral corticosteroids reduce nodule size. The effect is temporary, so corticosteroids are an alternative where surgery is not possible rather than a first choice.

evidence.reference_title: Juvenile Hyaline Fibromatosis: Literature Review and a Case Treated With Surgical Excision and Corticosteroid.

nodes.description: Collagen VI accumulates in the duodenal wall, demonstrated by electron microscopy and second harmonic generation imaging in affected patients. Intestinal organoids derived from a patient and CRISPR ANTXR2 knockout organoids grew and polarised normally and formed monolayers normally, so the epithelium itself is not primarily defective; the abnormality is in the matrix around it. This is the reason protein-losing enteropathy is placed downstream of matrix change rather than of epithelial failure.

evidence.reference_title: Enhanced Collagen Deposition in the Duodenum of Patients with Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome and Protein Losing Enteropathy.
evidence.snippet: electron microscopy and second harmonic generation imaging showed abnormal collagen deposition in duodenal samples of these patients

evidence.reference_title: Enhanced Collagen Deposition in the Duodenum of Patients with Hyaline Fibromatosis Syndrome and Protein Losing Enteropathy.
evidence.snippet: An intrinsic defect of monolayer formation in patient-derived or ANTXR2KO organoids was not apparent, suggesting normal epithelial function.

nodes.description: Ectodomain missense mutants fold incorrectly. Immunoglobulin-like domain substitutions prevent the correct disulphide bonds from forming. The misfolded protein is held in the endoplasmic reticulum and routed to ER-associated degradation, so it does not reach the plasma membrane. The block is partly reversible: proteasome inhibition in patient fibroblasts restores surface CMG2 that is signalling competent, which is what makes this step a candidate intervention point rather than simply a consequence.
nodes.id: Endoplasmic Reticulum Retention of Misfolded CMG2

evidence.reference_title: Hyaline fibromatosis syndrome inducing mutations in the ectodomain of anthrax toxin receptor 2 can be rescued by proteasome inhibitors.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the Ig-like domain prevent proper disulphide bond formation and are more efficiently targeted to ER-associated degradation.

nodes.description: Collagen VI, the physiological ligand of CMG2, builds up in the extracellular matrix. This is the material that histology reports as amorphous, eosinophilic, PAS-positive and diastase-resistant hyaline. That the accumulation is specifically collagen VI driven was shown by crossing Antxr2-null mice with Col6a1-null mice, which reverses the phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: FAPs orchestrate ANTXR2-mediated fine-tuning of collagen VI to ensure skeletal muscle function.
evidence.snippet: Using Antxr2-/-::Col6a1-/- double-knockout mice, we demonstrate that these phenotypes are COL6-dependent

evidence.reference_title: CMG2/ANTXR2 regulates extracellular collagen VI which accumulates in hyaline fibromatosis syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Crossing Antxr2-/- with Col6a1-/- mice leads to restoration of uterine structure and reversion of female infertility.

nodes.description: In the intact pathway, collagen VI binding releases talin from CMG2 in a src-dependent manner and recruits RhoA and its effectors, and this switch drives internalisation of the receptor with its ligand and subsequent intracellular degradation of collagen VI. Without the receptor the switch cannot occur and collagen VI is not cleared. Collagen VI gene expression is unchanged in Antxr2-null mice, so the defect is in removal rather than in production.

evidence.reference_title: Ligand Binding to the Collagen VI Receptor Triggers a Talin-to-RhoA Switch that Regulates Receptor Endocytosis.
evidence.snippet: CMG2 binds talin, and thereby the actin cytoskeleton, only in its ligand-free state. Extracellular ligand binding leads to src-dependent talin release and recruitment of the actin cytoskeleton regulator RhoA and its effectors.

nodes.description: A second, matrix-independent route to the gut phenotype, shown so far only in mouse. CMG2 knockout mice have a normal colon until colitis is induced; they then fail to regenerate the epithelium because the Wnt-dependent transition from fetal-like cells to Lgr5-positive adult stem cells is blocked, with defective beta-catenin nuclear translocation. The authors propose CMG2 as a context-specific modulator of Wnt signalling. Whether this operates in affected children has not been shown, so the human inference is explicit rather than demonstrated and the node is recorded with a knowledge gap attached.

nodes.description: Collagen VI accumulates within intramuscular connective tissue. In the mouse this stiffens the tissue and drives maladaptive muscle hypertrophy with impaired locomotion and myopathic features, and the phenotype is abolished by removing collagen VI. This is offered as the mechanistic basis for the muscle component of HFS; the human counterpart recorded in the clinical literature is weakness and hypotonia alongside the contractures.
